record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.original_question: Can one construct examples of cones D in a maximal R-split torus A with dim D≥3 that have no non-obvious divergent trajectories?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 26 (Barak Weiss). Construct examples of cones D in A with dim D ≥ 3 and no non-obvious divergent trajectories.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a connected semisimple real algebraic group defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, let $\Gamma \subset G$ be an arithmetic lattice, and assume $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}}(G) = \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb{R}}(G)$. Let $A \subset G$ be a maximal $\mathbb{R}$-split torus (which then contains a maximal $\mathbb{Q}$-split torus). A trajectory $\{a_t \cdot x : t \geq 0\}$ in $G/\Gamma$, generated by a one-parameter subsemigroup $\{a_t\}$ of $A$, is called divergent if for every compact $K \subset G/\Gamma$ there exists $T$ with $a_t \cdot x \notin K$ for all $t \geq T$. By a closed cone $D \subset A$ we mean a closed semigroup of the form $D = \{a \in T_0 : \chi_i(a) \geq 0,\ i=1,\dots,k\}$, where $T_0 \subset A$ is a closed connected subgroup and $\chi_1,\dots,\chi_k$ are characters of $T_0$. There is a finite, explicit list of algebraic mechanisms (coming from $\mathbb{Q}$-parabolic subgroups and $\mathbb{Q}$-characters) that produce divergent trajectories for the $D$-action on $G/\Gamma$; these are called obvious divergent trajectories. A divergent trajectory not arising from this list is called a non-obvious divergent trajectory.

Problem: Construct an example of a triple $(G,\Gamma,D)$ as above in which $\dim D \geq 3$ and the action of $D$ on $G/\Gamma$ admits no non-obvious divergent trajectories.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Tamam, 2021–2022) classifies non-obvious divergent trajectories in rational rank two and provides existence results showing non-obvious divergent trajectories arise when the diagonalizable subgroup has small dimension relative to the $\mathbb{Q}$-rank. No explicit construction of cones $D$ with $\dim D \geq 3$ free of non-obvious divergent trajectories appears in the literature, and the question is posed as an open construction problem.

status_evidence.title: Existence of non-obvious divergent trajectories in homogeneous spaces
status_evidence.snippet: If the projection of a diagonalizable subgroup A to any Q-factor of G is of small enough dimension (relatively to the Q-rank), then there are non-obvious divergent trajectories.
status_evidence.claim: Existence results give non-obvious divergent trajectories for low-dimensional cones; constructions avoiding them for dim D ≥ 3 are not given.

status_evidence.title: Divergent trajectories in arithmetic homogeneous spaces of rational rank two
status_evidence.snippet: Full classification of non-obvious divergent trajectories under the assumption rank_Q G = rank_R G = 2.
status_evidence.claim: Classification exists in rational rank 2; the cone construction in higher dimension remains open.
